item.title: Domain-specific dataset enable accurate MLIPs for disordered halide-based solid electrolytes
item.description:
📚 Machine Learning: Science and Technology
👤 Chiku Parida, Arghya Bhowmik and Juan Maria Garcia Lastra
Efficient exploration of chemical space with machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) requires a comprehensive, application-focused training database. Solid-state electrolytes for Li-ion batteries have attracted growing attention owing to their ability to improve safety and energy density. Among these, halide-based solid electrolytes have emerged as promising candidates because of their high ionic conductivity and stability. We present an MLIP training database for -type halide electrolytes, where M can be group-3, group-13, and group-15 elements as well as lanthanides, and X represents halogens. item.title: Gradient-based versus gradient-free optimization in hybrid quantum machine learning: a systematic benchmark
item.description:
📚 Machine Learning: Science and Technology
👤 Stefan Klug and Maximilian Moll
Hybrid quantum machine learning (QML) relies on quantum variational circuits (QVCs) trained together with classical components. While gradient-based training is standard, it is costly on near-term hardware and vulnerable to barren plateaus, motivating gradient-free alternatives. However, there is limited systematic evidence comparing gradient-free methods to strong gradient baselines under matched quantum-evaluation budgets. A benchmark of 15 gradient-based, gradient-free, and hybrid optimizers is conducted on four binary classification datasets and two three-qubit QVC architectures using a unified experimental protocol under a fixed per-step quantum-evaluation budget.
